output.question: What does Walmart's supply chain look like?
output.answer: Walmart is spending heavily to automate its supply chain. On October 29, 2026 it expanded its deal with Symbotic, committing about $6 billion over several years to add automation at 25 U.S. regional distribution centers, plus a separate $125 million for racking and picking R&D. According to its FY2026 10-K (fiscal year ended Jan 31, 2026), Walmart moves goods through 192 distribution facilities in the U.S. and 179 abroad (Africa, Canada, Central America, Chile, China, India and Mexico). Freight travels on its own private truck fleet and on contracted common carriers, and most store and club merchandise passes through these facilities. eCommerce orders ship from stores, clubs, eCommerce fulfillment centers and other distribution facilities. During fiscal 2026, Walmart also began folding the Sam's Club U.S. supply chain into Walmart U.S.'s. In April 2023 Walmart set a goal that by the end of FY2026 about 65% of stores would be served by automation and about 55% of fulfillment-center volume would flow through automated facilities.

key_facts.fact: On Oct 29 (2026), Walmart and Symbotic expanded their agreement: an initial commitment of about $6 billion to bring more automation to 25 U.S. regional distribution centers. Walmart also committed $125 million to racking and picking R&D.
Walmart uses 192 distribution facilities in the U.S. (FY2026 10-K).
Walmart uses 179 distribution facilities outside the U.S., in Africa, Canada, Central America, Chile, China, India and Mexico.
Freight moves on Walmart's private truck fleet plus contracted common carriers. eCommerce orders also ship from eCommerce fulfillment centers and other distribution facilities.
During fiscal 2026, Walmart began combining the Sam's Club U.S. supply chain function with Walmart U.S.

Walmart's April 2023 target for the end of FY2026: about 65% of stores served by automation, about 55% of fulfillment-center volume through automated facilities, and about 20% lower average cost per unit.

passages.quote: In the U.S., we utilize a network of 192 distribution facilities located strategically throughout the country
Outside the U.S., we utilize a total of 179 distribution facilities
using a combination of our private truck fleet as well as contracting with common carriers
we began combining the Sam's Club U.S. supply chain function with Walmart U.S.
roughly 65% of Walmart stores will be serviced by automation

caveats: The 10-K figures (192 U.S. and 179 international facilities) are as of fiscal year end Jan 31, 2026. The network may have changed since then.
The 65%/55% automation figures are a 2023 target. I did not find a primary source confirming whether Walmart actually hit them.

Secondary reports say about 60% of stores got freight from automated DCs as of Feb 2026, and that stores fulfilled about 80% of e-commerce orders per the Aug 2026 earnings call. I could not check these against primary transcripts, so they are left out of the answer.
Symbotic deal details come from trade press (Logistics Viewpoints), not from the primary Walmart or Symbotic release. The article does not say which Symbotic systems will go into each of the 25 DCs.
The 10-K was read only in part (the first 100k characters). It does not give a separate distribution-facility count for Sam's Club.
missing_fields: Actual end-of-FY2026 share of stores served by automated DCs (only the target was verified)
Separate Sam's Club U.S. distribution facility count
Primary Walmart/Symbotic press release for the Oct 2026 deal
